validity.researcher_notes:
ORCHESTRATOR ADJUDICATION 2026-09-14 — this SUPERSEDES the duplicate verdict this shard's row agent reached, and the matching verdict in the other row's shard. P3200 and P5990 are NOT the same project. They are two SUCCESSIVE, separately-filed Virginia Natural Gas applications to the Virginia SCC, and GEM has recorded them under the same name:
  (a) HEADER IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (HIP) — ~24 mi in three distinct pipelines: the 6.2 mi Transco Interconnect Pipeline (Quantico to Transco's mainline at Catlett, Fauquier Co), the 3.3 mi Quantico Parallel Pipe (Fauquier Co), and the 14.6 mi Mechanicsville Parallel Pipe (Hanover, New Kent and Charles City Cos) = 24.1 mi; ~$346M; 30 in. Sized for the proposed C4GT gas-fired plant in Charles City County, which supplied the bulk of the project's funding. DISMISSED by the Virginia SCC in December 2020 after VNG told the Commission the C4GT conditions would not be met by the Dec 31 deadline. => This is the project P5990's DATA describes (24 mi / 30 in / $346M / Prince William-Fauquier, and both of P5990's own live-sheet refs are Header-Improvement-Project pages).
  (b) VNG INTERCONNECT — the renamed, downsized successor, filed 2020-12-14, three days before HIP's dismissal took effect. ~10 mi (about 6 mi in Prince William Co + 4 mi in Fauquier Co), i.e. HIP's first two segments (6.2 + 3.3 = 9.5 mi) with the 14.6 mi Mechanicsville leg DROPPED; +245,000 Dth/d (~245 MMcf/d); $205M; plus a new compressor station near Nokesville and upgrades to the Hanover/Mechanicsville metering station. WITHDRAWN March 2021 as 'no longer needed as proposed'. => This is the project P3200's DATA describes, and it is EIA's single 'VNG Interconnect' row (Aug 2026, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 1143: 10 miles, 245 MMcf/d, $205M, VA, authority SCC).
The two scopes OVERLAP physically (the Interconnect re-proposes HIP's two northern segments) but they are separate applications with separate dockets, separate scopes, separate costs and separate dispositions, and EIA carries only the second. Merging or retiring either row would delete a real, separately-adjudicated project from the record. KEEP BOTH. The defects are naming and attribution, not duplication.

CORRECTION, and this SUPERSEDES the earlier UNRESOLVED on this unit. The sheet records Owner1='Transco' [100%] with Parent=Williams Companies. That is wrong. Virginia Natural Gas (parent: Southern Company) is the applicant, sponsor and owner; the Virginia SCC - a STATE regulator - is the authority, which is itself inconsistent with a Williams interstate project under FERC. Transco is the INTERCONNECT COUNTERPARTY: the new VNG lateral was to begin at a new interconnect station on Transco's existing mainline near the Prince William / Fauquier county line. EIA's own project_notes say exactly this - 'Pipeline expansion to an interconnect with Transco' - and that phrasing is the likely origin of GEM's mistaken Owner attribution, the same way the row was nested under PipelineNetworkGrouping 'Transcontinental Gas Pipeline'.
WHY THIS IS NO LONGER UNRESOLVED: the earlier pass left it UNRESOLVED under rule 5's exception - EIA's operator naming a different company from the sheet's Owner1 is a concern, not a confirmation. That was correct while EIA was the only origin. It no longer is: the Prince William Times reports the same ownership independently of EIA, so two independent origins now agree on the correct owner and the unit resolves as a sourced correction rather than a bare disagreement. Recommend Owner1='Virginia Natural Gas', Owner1%=100%, Parent='Southern Co' (P5990 already records exactly this for the sibling project).
